generic_sampling_rules.text_primary_key: Generate fresh unique values '<prefix><n>' with n a running integer; never NULL; no duplicates. Boundary pools for PK columns are deduplicated per instance and any boundary value that collides with a fresh value is suffixed with a running integer so uniqueness is preserved.
generic_sampling_rules.text_fk_column: Copy the value from the referenced parent row's final (post-dedup) column values; never NULL unless the column is nullable. For nullable FK columns, apply the NULL share AFTER all FK filling and duplicate-share enforcement so that each instance contains at least one NULL and at least one non-NULL value.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Sample uniformly from the explicit enum pool; near-variants (case changes, truncations, appended '%') only where listed in per_column_exceptions. Strict enum columns (bool.name, no_payment_due.bool, enlist.organ, enrolled.school) are constrained by their enum formula; boundary variants outside the enum domain are NOT generated for them.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Sample from a small pool of short strings; include near-duplicate variants (case flips, one-character truncation) at low rate.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_range: Sample integers uniformly within the stated range; include the boundary values and one step outside where listed.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_month: Sample integers 0..12; include 0 and the listed boundary values.
generic_sampling_rules.nullable_column: With the stated NULL share emit NULL; otherwise sample from the column domain. NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule. Each nullable column has at least one NULL row per instance.
generic_sampling_rules.join_orphans: For join columns, ensure some parent rows have no child rows and (where nullable) some child rows have NULL foreign keys.
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_duplicates: On DISTINCT-target columns allow 20-50% duplicate values across rows.
generic_sampling_rules.order_ties: On ORDER/LIMIT-target columns plant ties at the listed ranks. For value-order ties sort the column in the stated direction before planting. For aggregate-count ties (enlist.organ, enrolled.school) compute group counts, sort groups by count in the stated direction, and force the top group count to be shared by at least two groups (tie at rank 1).
generic_sampling_rules.table_size_variation: Use the exact table_sizes_per_instance values; no per-instance variation.

generation_specification.uncertainty: No calculated columns present; no date pairs; no numeric quantity/price columns beyond month. Formula checks limited to enum and range rules. Duplicate shares and tie ranks are approximate targets from the atomic summary. Numeric one-step boundary values (1,2,3) for enlist.name are intentionally dropped: the column is TEXT and numeric literals are type-mismatched; only string boundary values are generated. Comparison-boundary targets for strict enum columns (enlist.organ, enrolled.school, bool.name, no_payment_due.bool) are removed because they conflict with the enum formulas; only in-enum values are generated for those columns. Aggregate-count ties for enlist.organ and enrolled.school are defined as group-count ties at rank 1 (top count shared by >=2 groups). enrolled.month distinct=15 in the original is unreconciled with the chosen 0-12 range; 0-12 is confirmed. NULL shares for nullable columns are derived from the compact database with a floor of one NULL row per instance.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.valid = 0, validity.invalid = 20, reasons = {no_rows_added: 20, compact_rows_missing: 20}. All 20 generated instances contain no rows and the compact database rows are missing. In writer.py, write_instance_sqlite copies the compact DB only via `shutil.copyfile(schema.orig_path, part) if hasattr(schema, 'orig_path') else None`, but schema.py's Schema dataclass never sets an `orig_path` attribute (read_schema returns Schema(tables, fks, ddl, torder, corder, ov, sizes, from_index) with no orig_path). So the copy is skipped, the .part file is created empty by sqlite3.connect, and the generated rows are inserted into a fresh empty DB. Additionally, the generated rows themselves are not being written (no_rows_added), which is consistent with the empty base DB plus the fact that the writer inserts into tables that don't exist in the empty file (executemany fails, row-by-row also fails, all counted as bad).
issues.requested_revision: Set schema.orig_path in read_schema (or pass orig_path explicitly to write_instance_sqlite) so the compact database is actually copied before appending generated rows. Verify that after the fix, generated instances contain the compact rows plus the generated rows, and that validity.valid > 0.

issues.evidence: instance.py build_random_instance: `inst[t] = cols` is assigned BEFORE `cols.update(fill_foreign_keys_consistently(...))`, so the FK columns are added to a local `cols` dict that is then overwritten by `cols = sample_fresh_primary_keys(...)` and `cols = drop_unique_duplicates(...)`. The final `inst[t] = cols` at the end of the loop does include FK columns, but the intermediate `inst[t] = cols` assignment is dead and, more importantly, `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` reads `instance.get(pt, {}).get(pc)` — for a child table whose parent has already been processed this is fine, but the FK values are drawn from the parent's *pre-dedup* column list, so after `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` shrink the parent, some FK values may reference parent rows that were dropped. This can produce FK violations (the execution feedback reports fk_violations=0 only because no rows were written at all).
issues.requested_revision: Draw FK values from the parent's final (post-dedup) column values, i.e. fill FKs after the parent table's `inst[pt]` has been finalized, and re-validate that fk_violations stays 0 once rows are actually written.

issues.evidence: spec.py plant_ties: `out[rank] = out[rank - 1]` for rank in TIE_RANKS. For ('longest_absense_from_school','month') ranks [1,5], rank=1 sets out[1]=out[0] (tie at rank 1, ok), rank=5 sets out[5]=out[4] (tie at rank 5, ok). But for ('disabled','name') rank [5] this makes out[5]=out[4], which is a tie at rank 5 only if the list is sorted; the spec says 'tie at rank 5 ASC' on disabled.name, and the sampler does not sort before planting, so the planted tie is at an arbitrary position, not rank 5 of the ASC order. Similarly ('enlist','organ') rank [1] and ('enrolled','school') rank [1] plant a tie between positions 0 and 1 without regard to the COUNT-based ordering the spec describes ('tie at rank 1 on COUNT(enlist.organ)').
issues.requested_revision: Sort the column (or the relevant aggregate) before planting ties so the tie actually occurs at the specified rank in the specified direction, or document that tie ranks are approximate and adjust the spec accordingly.

issues.evidence: Specification null_rows: no_payment_due.bool '5-30% NULL rows', longest_absense_from_school.month 'nullable; include NULL rows'. The program interface rule (instruction 7) requires that for every nullable column each instance contains at least one NULL row and a NULL share following the compact database's share. The spec gives a fixed 5-30% range rather than deriving the share from the compact database, and does not state a minimum of one NULL row per instance. With small table sizes (e.g. disabled=20, unemployed=20) a 5% share can round to zero NULLs.
issues.requested_revision: State in the specification that the NULL share is derived from the compact database's observed NULL share for each nullable column (with a floor of at least one NULL row per instance), and that NOT NULL/PK columns never receive NULL. This aligns the spec with the program-interface NULL rule.

issues.evidence: Specification dependencies: `{'unique': 'enlist (name, organ)', 'note': 'no unique constraint; duplicates allowed'}`. The schema has no unique constraint on enlist(name, organ), and the note says duplicates are allowed, yet the entry is listed under 'dependencies' with a 'unique' key, which is contradictory and could mislead the engineer into enforcing uniqueness. Also `enrolled (name, school)` is correctly a composite PK.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the misleading 'unique' entry for enlist(name, organ) or relabel it as a non-unique composite; keep only the enrolled composite-PK uniqueness rule.

issues.evidence: Specification comparison_boundary for enlist.name includes 'student212','student210' and for longest_absense_from_school.name includes 'student347','student349', but the atomic summary's comparison_boundary targets for these columns list only ['student211','STUDENT211'] and ['student348','STUDENT348'] respectively (plus equal_and_one_step_from). The extra one-step values are plausible but not directly evidenced; they are an inference, not a supported rule.

issues.evidence: spec.py make_spec_sampler: for boundary columns (e.g. person.name, disabled.name) it returns BoundarySampler, which samples 35% from the boundary pool and otherwise fresh 'student%d' values. But person.name is a primary key and the spec's generic_sampling_rules.text_primary_key says 'Generate fresh unique values of the form <prefix><n>; never NULL; no duplicates.' The boundary pool contains duplicates (e.g. 'student214' and 'STUDENT214' are distinct, but the pool is reused across rows), and BoundarySampler does not guarantee uniqueness. sample_fresh_primary_keys later drops duplicate PK tuples, which will silently shrink person below its target size and may break FK references.
issues.requested_revision: For primary-key columns, ensure the sampler produces unique values (e.g. append a running integer suffix to boundary values, or deduplicate the boundary pool per instance) so that sample_fresh_primary_keys does not drop rows and FK references remain valid.

issues.evidence: instance.py choose_table_sizes varies each table size by ±20% around TABLE_SIZES, but the specification's table_sizes_per_instance gives exact sizes (bool:2, person:200, ...). The spec does not authorize per-instance variation. This is a deviation from the specification.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'no_payment_due.bool: generated rows: NULL 0 / 2092'. The specification (null_rows target for no_payment_due.bool) and the program interface NULL rule require at least one NULL row per instance for every nullable column, with a share following the compact database. The program's NullableEnumSampler is only selected when key in NULL_SHARES, and NULL_SHARES contains ('no_payment_due','bool'), so a NULL share should be drawn. However, no_payment_due.bool is a foreign key (schema.fks contains ('no_payment_due','bool') -> ('bool','name')), and in instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently overwrites the sampled column with values drawn from the parent's final values (never NULL), discarding the NULLs produced by the sampler. The _ensure_null step explicitly skips FK columns ('if (t, cm.name) in schema.fks: continue'). Result: zero NULLs in a nullable FK column across all instances.
issues.requested_revision: In instance.py, do not let fill_foreign_keys_consistently overwrite a nullable FK column's NULLs. Either (a) sample the FK column with the nullable sampler and only fill non-NULL entries from the parent, or (b) after FK filling, re-apply the NULL share for nullable FK columns (e.g. set a fraction of rows to NULL, guaranteeing at least one NULL per instance) while keeping the remaining values as valid parent references. Ensure the NULL share follows the compact database's observed share for no_payment_due.bool.

issues.evidence: spec.py LIKE_VARIANTS for ('enlist','organ') is ['%marines%','%air_force%','%navy%'], but the specification's like_near_variant target is ['%marines%','%air_force%','%navy%'] — this matches. However, EnumWithBoundarySampler for enlist.organ samples LIKE variants at 10% and boundary variants at 20%, while the specification's text_enum rule says 'near-variants (case changes, truncations, appended %) only where listed in per_column_exceptions' and the semantic rule for enlist.organ is 'organ IN (fire_department, air_force, navy, marines, foreign_legion, army, peace_corps)'. The boundary pool for enlist.organ includes 'AIR_FORCE','FOREIGN_LEGION','NAVY' and LIKE variants '%marines%' etc., which violate the semantic enum rule (organ must be one of the 7 lowercase values). The specification lists these as comparison_boundary targets, but the semantic_rules_and_formulas section states organ IN (7 values). This is an internal inconsistency in the specification that the program implements literally, producing values that violate the stated semantic rule.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: reconcile the specification — either the semantic rule for enlist.organ should permit the boundary/LIKE variants (and the rule should be stated as such), or the comparison_boundary/like_near_variant targets for enlist.organ should be removed. Engineer: once reconciled, ensure the sampler does not emit values outside the permitted domain. Same concern applies to enrolled.school (boundary pool includes 'OCC','ULCA','' and 'x' vs semantic rule school IN (6 lowercase values)) and no_payment_due.bool (boundary pool includes 'e','E','g','G' vs semantic rule bool IN ('neg','pos')).

issues.evidence: spec.py TIE_RANKS for ('longest_absense_from_school','month') is [1,5] and apply_column_rules uses direction 'DESC' for this key. The specification says 'ties at ranks 1 and 5, DESC and unordered'. plant_ties sorts DESC then sets out[rank]=out[rank-1] for rank in [1,5]. For rank=1, out[1]=out[0] — this creates a tie at rank 1 (positions 1 and 2 in 1-based terms, i.e., the top two values equal). For rank=5, out[5]=out[4]. This is a reasonable interpretation, but note the specification also says 'unordered' for this column, which the program does not separately handle (it always sorts). Minor.
issues.requested_revision: Optional: document or implement the 'unordered' aspect of the tie target for longest_absense_from_school.month, or confirm that sorting DESC is the intended interpretation. Not blocking.

issues.evidence: instance.py build_random_instance applies apply_column_rules (duplicates and ties) to sampled columns BEFORE fill_foreign_keys_consistently overwrites FK columns. For FK columns that are also in DUP_SHARES (e.g., enlist.name, disabled.name, male.name, etc.), the duplicate planting is discarded because the FK fill replaces the entire column with parent values drawn with replacement. The duplicate share is then determined by the parent's value distribution, not by the specified 20-50% target. This may or may not achieve the target duplicate share depending on parent size vs child size (e.g., person has 200 rows, enlist has 60 rows — drawing 60 from 200 with replacement gives ~14% expected duplicates, below the 20-50% target).
issues.requested_revision: After FK filling, verify or enforce the duplicate share for FK columns listed in DUP_SHARES (e.g., by biasing the draw toward repeated parent values, or by post-processing to plant duplicates). Alternatively, document that FK duplicate shares are governed by parent cardinality and adjust the specification's duplicate targets for FK columns accordingly.

unresolved_checks: Whether the duplicate share for FK columns (enlist.name, disabled.name, male.name, unemployed.name, no_payment_due.name, enrolled.name, filed_for_bankrupcy.name) actually reaches the specified 20-50% target after FK filling — not directly measured in the feedback.

Whether the tie at rank 1 for enlist.organ and enrolled.school (aggregate COUNT ties) is actually realized, since plant_ties operates on the raw column values, not on aggregate counts. The specification says 'tie at rank 1 on COUNT(enlist.organ)' and 'tie at rank 1 on COUNT(*)' — planting ties on the column values does not guarantee a tie in the aggregate count ranking. This is a potential mismatch between the specification's aggregate-tie intent and the program's value-level tie planting.

Whether the 'rows_with_different_values' target for longest_absense_from_school.month ('at least 2 rows per group with different month values') is satisfied — the program does not implement any grouping logic for this target.

issues.title: no_payment_due.bool never receives NULL values despite being a declared nullable column with a NULL rule
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'no_payment_due.bool: generated rows: NULL 0 / 2100'. The specification lists no_payment_due.bool in null_targets and per_column_exceptions null_rows ('NULL share derived from compact database observed share; at least one NULL row per instance'). The program's NullableEnumSampler does emit NULL with probability null_share, but instance.py then overwrites the column: fill_foreign_keys_consistently() treats no_payment_due.bool as an FK to bool.name and replaces every value with rng.choice(parent_values) (never NULL). The re-application of NULL share in instance.py only runs for keys in NULL_SHARES, which does include ('no_payment_due','bool'), so _apply_null_share should fire — yet the observed output is 0 NULLs. The likely cause is ordering: after _apply_null_share, the FK duplicate-share enforcement (DUP_SHARES does not contain this key, so not it) or the PK/UNIQUE dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys on no_payment_due.name) drops rows, but more importantly the NULLs are set on fk_cols[cm.name] and then cols.update(fk_cols) — however the subsequent 'enforce at least one NULL row for nullable non-FK columns' loop skips FK columns, and the earlier _apply_null_share path is the only one. Regardless of the exact mechanism, the empirical result is 0 NULLs across 2100 rows, contradicting the spec's 'at least one NULL row per instance' and the program-interface NULL rule. This is a concrete, reproducible defect.
issues.requested_revision: Fix instance.py so that for nullable FK columns (no_payment_due.bool) the NULL share is applied AFTER all FK filling and duplicate-share enforcement, and verify with a unit test that each generated instance contains at least one NULL and at least one non-NULL value in no_payment_due.bool. Re-run generation and confirm the feedback line shows a non-zero NULL count.

issues.title: Comparison-boundary pools for strict enum columns are unreachable, leaving boundary targets unimplemented
issues.evidence: spec.py defines BOUNDARY_POOLS for ('enlist','organ') = ['air_force','AIR_FORCE','foreign_legion','FOREIGN_LEGION','navy','NAVY','Foreign Legion','foreign legion'] and ('enrolled','school') = ['occ','OCC','ulca','ULCA','','x'], and ('bool','name')/('no_payment_due','bool') with case variants. But STRICT_ENUM_COLUMNS marks all four as strict, and EnumWithBoundarySampler with strict=True filters boundary to values already in the enum pool and drops LIKE variants entirely. The specification's comparison_boundary targets for these columns (e.g. 'AIR_FORCE', 'Foreign Legion', 'ulca', 'x', 'OCC') are therefore never generated. The specification itself is internally inconsistent: it lists these boundary values as targets while also declaring strict enum formulas (organ IN (...), school IN (...), bool IN ('neg','pos')). The program resolves the conflict by silently discarding the boundary targets, so the specification's stated comparison_boundary targets for these columns are not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: reconcile the specification — either remove the out-of-enum comparison_boundary targets for strict enum columns (organ, school, bool) and the LIKE near-variants for enlist.organ, or relax the enum formulas to permit the boundary variants. Engineer: implement whichever resolution is chosen and document it. As written, the spec's comparison_boundary targets for enlist.organ, enrolled.school, bool.name and no_payment_due.bool are not realized.

issues.title: Tie planting for aggregate-based ties (enlist.organ, enrolled.school) is not implemented as specified
issues.evidence: Specification ties_for_order_limit: enlist.organ 'tie at rank 1 on COUNT(enlist.organ), ASC and DESC (sort by aggregate before planting)'; enrolled.school 'tie at rank 1 on COUNT(*), DESC (sort by aggregate before planting)'. spec.py TIE_RANKS includes these keys, but apply_column_rules calls plant_ties on the raw column values, which sorts the column values themselves, not the group-by aggregate counts. For a low-cardinality enum column (7 organs, 6 schools) the notion of 'rank 1 on COUNT' is about group counts, not value order, so plant_ties cannot produce the specified tie. The tie is effectively meaningless for these columns. This is a specification/program mismatch: the spec asks for aggregate-rank ties that the program does not compute.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: either implement aggregate-count tie planting (compute group counts, sort groups by count, force a tie at the specified rank) or, if the intent is only to guarantee that the top group count is shared, document and implement that. Designer: clarify the intended semantics of 'tie at rank 1 on COUNT(...)' for enum columns so the program can implement it deterministically.

issues.title: Uncertain / unevidenced rules flagged in the specification's own uncertainty note
issues.evidence: The specification's 'uncertainty' field states: 'One-step-away boundary values for enlist.name and longest_absense_from_school.name are inferred and not directly evidenced; boundary pools restricted to evidenced values.' The atomic summary lists comparison_boundary targets for enlist.name including values [1,2,3,'student211','STUDENT211'] and for longest_absense_from_school.name ['student348','STUDENT348'], but the specification's BOUNDARY_POOLS only include the string values, dropping the numeric one-step values (1,2,3). This is a deliberate, documented restriction and is acceptable, but it means the numeric boundary targets in the atomic summary are not implemented. This is a supported-rule gap rather than an error, but should be recorded.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: confirm that dropping the numeric one-step boundary values for enlist.name is intentional (the column is TEXT and numeric literals are likely type-mismatched). If so, note it explicitly in the specification so the reviewer can treat it as a supported decision rather than an omission. No program change required if confirmed.

issues.title: enrolled.month duplicate share and range are applied but month values are not constrained to the observed 1-8 range
issues.evidence: Specification supporting_evidence: 'enrolled.month: sample rows show months 1-8; statistics distinct=15; range 0-12 chosen'. The program uses INT_RANGES ('enrolled','month') = (0,12) and MonthSampler, which is consistent with the chosen range. However, the atomic summary reports enrolled.month distinct=15 in the original, while the spec's chosen range 0-12 yields at most 13 distinct values; the duplicate share (20-50%) further reduces distinctness. This is a minor inconsistency between the stated evidence (distinct=15) and the chosen domain (0-12), but the spec explicitly chose 0-12, so the program is faithful to the spec. Noted as an unresolved check rather than a blocking error.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: reconcile the 'distinct=15' evidence with the chosen 0-12 range (either widen the range or correct the evidence note). No program change required if the 0-12 range is confirmed.

unresolved_checks: The exact mechanism by which no_payment_due.bool NULLs are lost was not traced line-by-line; the empirical 0/2100 result is the evidence. The engineer should trace and fix.
Whether the aggregate-rank tie semantics for enlist.organ and enrolled.school are intended to be about group counts or value order is ambiguous in the specification.
The numeric one-step boundary values (1,2,3) for enlist.name in the atomic summary are not implemented; the specification documents this as intentional but it is not confirmed by the designer.
enrolled.month distinct=15 in the original vs. chosen 0-12 range is unreconciled.
reviews.summary: The program runs cleanly (20/20 instances, 0 FK/NOT NULL/PK violations, reproducible) and implements most of the specification: table sizes, enum pools, integer ranges, duplicate shares, boundary pools for text PKs, and FK consistency. However, there is a concrete defect: no_payment_due.bool receives zero NULL values across all generated rows, violating the specification's null_rows rule and the program-interface NULL rule. Additionally, the specification is internally inconsistent for strict enum columns (comparison_boundary targets outside the enum domain are silently dropped), and aggregate-rank tie planting for enlist.organ/enrolled.school is not implemented as specified. These warrant a revise.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: `no_payment_due.bool: generated rows: NULL 0 / 2064`. The specification (null_rows target for no_payment_due.bool) and the program interface NULL rule require at least one NULL row per instance for every nullable column, including nullable FKs. The spec.py revision note claims this was fixed ('previous round produced 0 NULLs because the FK fill overwrote the sampler's NULLs and the re-application path was not reached for this key'), but the execution still shows 0 NULLs across 20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the nullable-FK NULL path so no_payment_due.bool actually receives NULLs. In instance.py, the re-application loop guards on `key in NULL_SHARES` and `key in fk_cols`; verify that `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` populates no_payment_due.bool (it is an FK to bool.name) and that `_apply_null_share` is reached. Note that `_apply_null_share` sets `n_null = max(1, int(n*share))` but then `enforce_duplicate_share` runs afterward and can overwrite the planted NULLs (it copies values from random positions, including non-NULL ones, into the NULL slots). Reorder so NULL application is the final step for nullable FK columns, or make enforce_duplicate_share NULL-preserving. Add an assertion/check that each nullable column has >=1 NULL per instance.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback `rows_skipped` is large: person 326, male 510, no_payment_due 543, enrolled 1160, longest_absense_from_school 376, etc. The writer falls back to row-by-row inserts and counts failures, but the spec's `table_sizes_per_instance` are exact ('Use the exact table_sizes_per_instance values; no per-instance variation'). With person=200 and 20 instances, expected person rows = 4000, but only 2523 were added and 326 skipped; enrolled expected 4800, added 2937, skipped 1160. The generated instances therefore do not match the specified table sizes.
issues.requested_revision: Investigate why rows are skipped (likely PK/UNIQUE collisions after dedup, or NOT NULL/FK failures) and make generation produce the exact specified row counts per table per instance. The dedup steps (`sample_fresh_primary_keys`, `drop_unique_duplicates`) shrink tables below target sizes; the spec requires exact sizes, so the sampler must generate enough distinct PK/unique values to hit the target after dedup (e.g., draw fresh unique PKs rather than sampling-then-dropping).

issues.evidence: spec.py `plant_aggregate_tie` is invoked from `apply_column_rules` for enlist.organ and enrolled.school, but `apply_column_rules` is called in instance.py only for non-FK columns (`if cm.name in cols` where cols excludes FK columns). enlist.organ and enrolled.school are not FKs, so this path is reached — however, the aggregate tie is computed on the column values in isolation, before the table's other columns and before any dedup. More importantly, the spec's aggregate tie is on `COUNT(enlist.organ)` / `COUNT(*)` grouped by organ/school; planting a tie on the raw column distribution is a reasonable proxy, but the spec also requires `enrolled.school` tie on `COUNT(*)` (row count per school) which equals the column distribution only if every row has a school — which holds. This is acceptable, but the tie is planted before `plant_duplicates` may re-shuffle values? Order in apply_column_rules: duplicates first, then ties, then aggregate tie — so aggregate tie runs last, good. No blocking issue here; noting for completeness.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; confirm aggregate tie survives the final dedup steps (sample_fresh_primary_keys / drop_unique_duplicates) which run after apply_column_rules and could remove rows and break the planted tie.

issues.evidence: Specification `comparison_boundary` for enlist.name includes numeric values [1,2,3] and the atomic ops include `PRED(enlist.name >= 2)`.
